text.title: Conversion Tracking Failure Modes
text.summary: Six antipatterns observed when applying Conversion Tracking. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix. Detector clauses make them mechanically catchable.

antipattern.symptom: Ads Manager or GA4 reports roughly twice the purchases the order table shows; ROAS looks excellent; refreshing the thank-you page adds another purchase.

root-cause.source: Meta Conversions API documentation, deduplication; GA4 recommended events reference

antipattern.root-cause: Browser pixel and server event were sent without a shared `event_id` / `transaction_id`, or the purchase event fires on every load of the confirmation URL.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rules `r-monetary-conversion-carries-transaction-id` and `r-browser-server-dedup-and-identifiers`: one order id per purchase, reused as the event id in every destination; fire the purchase once and mark it in session storage.

antipattern.symptom: Reports show `sign_up`, `signup` and `SignUp` as three events; the funnel report has gaps; a rename in one codebase breaks a dashboard nobody knew depended on it.
antipattern.root-cause: No single registry; each team named events in code; nothing in CI checked the names.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-event-registry-single-source`: add `events.yml`, run `validate-events.py` in CI, and treat an unregistered name as a failed build.

antipattern.symptom: Cookies from analytics and ads vendors are set on first paint before the banner is answered; Google Ads shows the EEA conversion warning; the DPA complaint quotes the cookie list.
antipattern.root-cause: Consent defaults were never pushed before the config call, or the server container forwarded events regardless of consent state.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-consent-state-before-any-tag`: consent defaults with all four v2 signals precede the tag configuration; verify in the QA fixture that no vendor cookie exists before consent.

antipattern.symptom: After enabling server-side tracking, GA4 new users double, sessions per user fall to one, and every server-sent conversion attributes to `(direct) / (none)`.
antipattern.root-cause: The server generated a UUID for `client_id` instead of reading the `_ga` cookie, and omitted `session_id`.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-browser-server-dedup-and-identifiers`: pass the browser's `client_id` and `session_id` with every Measurement Protocol hit; forward `_fbp` and `_fbc` to Meta.

antipattern.symptom: An email address appears in `page_location` on the confirmation page or in a custom parameter; the GA property receives a policy warning; hashed matching to ad platforms fails because raw values were sent.

root-cause.source: Google Analytics Help, 'Best practices to avoid sending Personally Identifiable Information'

antipattern.root-cause: Confirmation URLs carried the email as a query parameter; the validation script only checked event names, not payload content.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-no-pii-in-parameters`: strip identifying query parameters before the page_view fires, hash matching identifiers with SHA-256, and add a payload check to the fixtures.

antipattern.symptom: Tracking is signed off from Chrome DevTools; a month later Safari and Firefox users show near-zero conversions and attribution windows collapse to one day.

root-cause.source: WebKit, Intelligent Tracking Prevention; Mozilla, Enhanced Tracking Protection

antipattern.root-cause: Fixtures were run once in one browser; the server endpoint sat on a vendor domain so ITP treated it as third-party anyway.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rules `r-qa-fixtures-per-tracking-change` and `r-server-endpoint-first-party-domain`: three browsers plus an ad-blocker profile per change, endpoint on a first-party subdomain, results recorded with the change.

section.title: Human checkpoint
section.p: Before any binding action driven by a Conversion Tracking output (publishing a container, enabling a conversion action for bidding, changing consent defaults), a named human reviewer must sign off. The agent surfaces a `ready_for_review=true` flag and does NOT auto-commit decisions, copy, configs, or rollouts.
